full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff-petitioner briefly stated, is that the suit premise belonged to pro-forma Defendant No. 6 Madan Mohan Jiew Deity. The plaintiff with the permission of the sebait of the Jiew. Constructed a shop house on the suit land and since then was running a grocery shop therein. Principal defendant having no right title interest and possession of the suit land asked the plaintiff through sebait to vacate the suit premises. Thus the plaintiff was constrained to bring the suit and to file an application for temporary injunction. 

 4. Defendant No. 1, the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet contested the suit by filing a written objection denying the material allegation of the plaintiff and contending, inter alia, that the suit land including other land known as Balaganj Bazar has been classified as hat and the same vested in the government under section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 as non retainable khas land of the ex-rent receiver and is under management of the Government and the said Bazar including the suit premises has been leased out to the Union Parishad for a period of 9 years for collection of toll; that the plaintiff has created some fraudulent documents with a view to grab the suit property and that the sebait is not entitled to lease out any debottar property as per provisions of section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and that the application for temporary injunction is liable to be rejected.
